questions.explanation: ACROPHOBIA — Greek 'akron' = peak, 'phobos' = fear. FEAR OF HEIGHTS. Common phobia (~5% of population). Symptoms: dizziness, sweating, panic when on tall building, balcony, cliff. ROOT 'acro' also in: ACROBAT (one who walks on heights), ACROPOLIS ('high city' — the citadel of ancient Athens), ACRONYM (top of words). PHOBIA SUFFIX: from Greek god PHOBOS (fear), brother of DEIMOS (terror). MASTER LIST OF PHOBIAS to learn (PYQ favourites): ACRO (heights), AGORA (open spaces), CLAUSTRO (closed spaces), HYDRO (water), PYRO (fire), NYCTO (darkness), THANATO (death), HEMO (blood), ARACHNO (spiders), OPHIDIO (snakes), CYNO (dogs), ZOO (animals), XENO (foreigners), GLOSSO (public speaking), TRISKAIDEKA (number 13).

questions.stem: XENOPHOBIA is the fear / hatred of:
questions.explanation: XENOPHOBIA — Greek 'xenos' = stranger / foreigner. Fear or hatred of foreigners / strangers / what is foreign. SOCIAL/POLITICAL phenomenon as much as personal phobia — anti-immigrant sentiment, racism. Same root: XENON (a noble gas — discovered + named because it's 'strange/foreign'), XENOGRAFT (transplant from one species to another), XENIAL (relating to hospitality, Greek custom toward strangers). RELATED phobias: ETHNOPHOBIA (fear of certain ethnic groups), HOMOPHOBIA (fear / prejudice against gay people — 'homos' = same; also 'homo' = same in homosexual). Greek roots are ESSENTIAL for English vocabulary; ~25% of English words trace to Greek roots.

questions.stem: HYDROPHOBIA is fear of WATER. It is also a CLINICAL SIGN of which disease?
questions.explanation: HYDROPHOBIA — fear of water. CLASSIC SYMPTOM of LATE-STAGE RABIES (caused by Lyssavirus, transmitted by infected animal bites — dogs primarily, also bats, monkeys, foxes). Patient unable to drink water due to painful throat spasms triggered by sight/sound of water. Once symptoms appear, rabies is almost 100% FATAL (no cure). PREVENTION: post-exposure VACCINATION (within hours/days of bite). India has world's highest rabies deaths (~36% of global deaths). Govt's STREET DOG vaccination + 'CARE OF STRAY' programs ongoing. INSIGHT — Louis Pasteur developed first rabies vaccine 1885 (saved 9-yr-old Joseph Meister, bitten by rabid dog). Pasteur Institute in India = primary rabies-vaccine producer; centres at Coonoor, Pune, Kolkata.

questions.explanation: GLOSSOPHOBIA — Greek 'glossa' = tongue. Fear of PUBLIC SPEAKING. World's MOST COMMON phobia (~75% of people experience some level). Often topped Jerry Seinfeld's joke: 'people fear public speaking more than death — at a funeral, you'd rather be in the casket than giving the eulogy.' Same root: POLYGLOT (knows many languages), GLOSSARY (list of language words), GLOSSITIS (inflamed tongue), HIEROGLYPHICS (sacred writing). RELATED phobias: TROPHOPHOBIA (fear of trophies — anxiety about success!); ATYCHIPHOBIA (fear of failure); SOCIAL anxiety disorder = broader umbrella. TREATMENT: cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), graded exposure, public-speaking clubs (Toastmasters), beta-blockers for performance anxiety.

questions.stem: TRISKAIDEKAPHOBIA is the unusual fear of:
questions.explanation: TRISKAIDEKAPHOBIA — Greek 'tris' (three) + 'kai' (and) + 'deka' (ten) = thirteen + 'phobia'. Fear / superstition around number 13. Many buildings skip floor 13 (go from 12 to 14). FRIDAY THE 13TH is considered unlucky in Western culture (subject of Hollywood horror franchise). Origin: possibly Last Supper (13 attended; Judas Iscariot = 13th, betrayed Jesus); or Norse mythology (Loki = 13th god, caused Balder's death). PARASKEVIDEKATRIAPHOBIA = fear specifically of Friday the 13th. INDIAN SUPERSTITION: avoid number 7 in some contexts (Saturday = Shani); 8 in others. ALSO EXAM-WORTHY phobias: COULROPHOBIA (clowns), TRYPOPHOBIA (clusters of holes), NOMOPHOBIA (fear of being WITHOUT MOBILE phone — modern!), PHILOPHOBIA (fear of love).

questions.explanation: ARACHNOPHOBIA — Greek 'arachne' = spider. Fear of spiders. ORIGIN of name: GREEK MYTH — Arachne, a mortal weaver, challenged goddess Athena to weaving contest, won; Athena turned her into a spider in punishment (or out of pity). Hence ARACHNIDS = class including spiders, scorpions, ticks, mites (8 legs). Spiders can be deadly (Black Widow, Brown Recluse, Sydney Funnel-Web), but most are harmless to humans. India has Trapdoor spiders, scorpions; check shoe before wearing in rural areas. Common: ENTOMOPHOBIA (insects); MUSOPHOBIA (mice); CYNOPHOBIA (dogs); AILUROPHOBIA (cats); OPHIDIOPHOBIA (snakes); APHENPHOSMPHOBIA (touch).

questions.stem: NOMOPHOBIA, a modern phobia, is the fear of:
questions.explanation: NOMOPHOBIA — coined 2008 in UK study; from 'NO MObile PHone phobia'. Fear of being without mobile phone / unable to use it. Symptoms: anxiety when phone battery dies, no signal, left phone at home. ~70% of smartphone users show signs. SAME ERA: FOMO ('Fear Of Missing Out' — anxiety about events / news on social media missed); SCREEN ADDICTION; PHANTOM POCKET VIBRATION. Modern phobias also: SELFITIS (compulsive selfie-taking — APA recognised); TECHNOPHOBIA (fear of technology). PHILOSOPHICAL angle — these aren't classical phobias but reflect modern anxieties tied to tech dependence. Cures: digital detox, screen-time limits, mindfulness. INDIA: highest mobile-phone usage globally; ~700 million smartphone users.
